key_insight: Replacing Cr with Cu in MnFeCoNi high-entropy alloys strengthens bifunctional alkaline water-splitting performance by tuning surface chemistry and reaction-intermediate binding.
engineering_relevance: A single-element substitution can be used as a practical design lever to create cheaper, higher-activity HEA electrocatalysts for hydrogen and oxygen evolution.
method: Compared CrMnFeCoNi (HEA-Cr) against MnFeCoNiCu (HEA-Cu) under the same alkaline HER/OER conditions.
Used electrochemical performance metrics including overpotential and Tafel slope to assess catalytic activity.
Supported experiments with computational electronic-structure analysis of H*, O*, OH*, and OOH* binding.
evidence_signal: HEA-Cu outperformed HEA-Cr for both HER and OER, reaching a lower overpotential of 538 mV and a Tafel slope of 165 mV dec-1, with simulations indicating more favorable intermediate binding.
watch_item: The Cu-rich surface formed after OER suggests the catalyst may undergo composition changes during operation, so durability and long-term stability should be verified.
paper_title: Structure-Property Correlation of Cr/Cu-MnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloys for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
